subject: Physiology
title: Renal Physiology: Countercurrent Mechanism & Acid-Base
preview: The nephron concentrates urine through loop countercurrent multiplication, vascular exchange and hormone-regulated water permeability.

sections.title: Countercurrent multiplier
points: Different permeabilities in descending and ascending nephron segments create the medullary gradient.
The thick ascending limb reabsorbs NaCl without accompanying water, diluting tubular fluid.

sections.title: Exchange and hormonal control
points: Vasa recta preserve the gradient through countercurrent exchange while minimizing solute washout.
ADH increases collecting duct water permeability through aquaporin regulation.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Loop of Henle segments are not uniformly water-permeable.
Concentrating ability depends on both the gradient and the collecting duct response to ADH.

quickRevision: The descending thin limb is relatively water-permeable, while the thick ascending limb reabsorbs salts and is water-impermeable.
The medullary osmotic gradient facilitates water reabsorption in the collecting system when antidiuretic hormone acts.
Urea recycling contributes to the inner medullary osmotic gradient.

quiz.question: Which structure is important in the renal countercurrent multiplier?
quiz.explanation: Countercurrent Multiplier & Exchanger: • Countercurrent Multiplier: Handled by the Loop of Henle.
